identity.title: Breaking Barriers: Combinatorial Algorithms for Non-Monotone Submodular Maximization with Sublinear Adaptivity and $1/e$ Approximation
identity.authors: Yixin Chen; Wenjing Chen; Alan Kuhnle
identity.page_convention: PDF page numbers, one-based, matching printed pages unless stated.

summary: Printed Algorithm2 violates its approximation theorem; UPDATE nontermination invalidates core parallel complexity/return claims; separate release distributor defect.
limitations: Some appendix proofs not exhaustively checked

problems.title: Algorithm2 permanently deletes useful unchosen elements
problems.assumptions: Nonnegative modular f(S)=|S intersect H|; n10000,k1000,ell10,epsilon.1; all theorem conditions checked
problems.check: Analytic all-branch invariant; auxiliary and independent parent integer simulations
problems.result: Every branch returns100 <267.879441; Lemma3.2 would require0>=90
problems.counterevidence: Resetting V to U minus G plausibly intended; parallel release reconstructs candidate set
problems.impact: Demonstrated false guarantee for core simplified algorithm as printed
problems.core_dependency: Section3 simplification and Lemma3.2 underpin claimed approximation and parallel development
problems.correction: Reset candidates per outer round; local witness repaired but complete theorem not certified

focused_check.note: Verified the modular n=10000, k=1000, ell=10, epsilon=0.1 witness satisfies theorem hypotheses. Permanent candidate deletion makes every branch return 100 versus the claimed 267.879... lower bound. The missing availability invariant is central, supporting Major. Resetting the pool fixes this witness only; the released parallel implementation is not alleged to share the serial defect.

problems.title: UPDATE cutoff is outside a nonterminating inner loop
problems.claim: PIG/PItG return in finite stated adaptive/query complexity
problems.assumptions: Singleton modular objective; legal n8,k2,ell2,epsilon.1 and main n20000,k1000,ell20,epsilon.1
problems.check: Exact positivity q^r>0 for all finite r, source visual checks and parent Fraction cutoff calculations
problems.result: Remaining marginals0 imply UPDATE never returns; caller cutoff unreachable
problems.counterevidence: Pinned source Pig::update has internal tau_min guard; same released infinite loop not alleged
problems.impact: False termination/query/adaptivity claims for central published algorithm
problems.core_dependency: Theorems4.1 and4.2 rely on shared UPDATE
problems.correction: Pass cutoff into UPDATE and return below it; only local correction verified

focused_check.note: Verified the cutoff is tested only after UPDATE returns; with zero remaining gains its positive threshold sequence never terminates in exact arithmetic. The main parallel call has the same obstruction. This invalidates core termination/query guarantees and supports Major. The release's internal tau_min guard is explicit counterevidence, so no empirical hang is alleged.

problems.title: Pinned Pig::dist never populates exclusion set
problems.claim: Released distributor returns pairwise disjoint candidate subsets
problems.assumptions: ell2; both pools0,1,2,3; legal cardinality and initial modular instance
problems.check: Static source read and independent finite semantic witness; no author code
problems.counterevidence: Paper's mathematical Algorithm3 has exclusion; release historical experiment link unresolved
problems.impact: Release does not satisfy proved invariant on witness; final objective loss unmeasured
problems.core_dependency: Disjointness is required for implementation-to-proof correspondence
problems.correction: Insert chosen items into exclusion set; whole-program repair unverified

focused_check.note: Verified Pig::dist declares and checks the exclusion set but never inserts selected elements, producing overlapping {0,1} from two admissible {0,1,2,3} pools. This is a Minor static release defect. It does not refute the mathematical distributor or establish historical experiment failure.

repair_verification: Candidate reset and internal cutoff repair exhibited witnesses only; no full repaired theorem/program certified.
